newsitem.title: USA: Perry says does not presume new Bosnia force needed.
newsitem.headline: Perry says does not presume new Bosnia force needed.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Wednesday he did not presume that U.S. and other international peacekeepers will have to go back into Bosnia next year to preserve peace there.

"I do not accept the presumption ... that we are going back with a second mission in January," Perry told the Senate Armed Services Committee. "I think that sending an American unit back in there next year will pose a very substantial problem."
Perry said elections in Bosnia over the weekend made him more confident than ever that the present NATO peacekeeping force including U.S. troops will leave at the end of the year.

"If I had any question about that it was whether there might be some major altercation occur at the elections," he said. "We're now past the elections so I have some confidence now in saying that that mission will be completed by the end of the year."
Perry said earlier this year that he believed a new Bosnia peace force would be needed next year if that was the only way to prevent new war and said he would recommend Americans be part of it.
But Perry said in July his assumption was that any renewed war threat in Bosnia next year could be stopped with air power and would not require a new peacekeeping force on the ground.

He told the senators that NATO defence ministers will begin discussing at a meeting next week in Bergen, Norway, whether a new international force will be needed for Bosnia next year and said "the outcome of that discussion is not at all clear."
"I have neither an open or covert conclusion on that question," he said. "I want to see how the analysis goes, what the facts on the ground are."
